correctness.rationale: The first sketch imposes r₀ᵀr₁=0 and gives r₁=(I−αA²)r₀ with α=||r₀||²/(r₀ᵀA²r₀). Put P=a², Q=b² and s=P cos²θ+Q sin²θ. In the eigenbasis the relative norm is (κ²−1)t/(κ²+t²) with t=|tan θ|; differentiation gives the maximum at t=κ for κ>1, with zero residual for κ=1. As an independent check on the angular mean, the squared relative norm is (P+Q)/s−PQ/s²−1. Integrating over uniform θ gives E[1/s]=1/√(PQ) by the tangent substitution, and differentiating with a common shift in P,Q gives E[1/s²]=(P+Q)/(2(PQ)^(3/2)). Thus the mean is (κ−1)²/(2κ). The strict increase set is between the two positive roots of t²−(κ²−1)t+κ² when κ>1+√2. Integrating the half-Cauchy direction law and using the root product κ² gives the stated arctangent and limit; the event is empty at equality and below. If r₁≠0, the orthogonal r₀,r₁ span the plane and force r₂=0 in the next exact sketch projection. Eigenvalue signs disappear through A².
